historical_references.reference: Beigh was a Rajput clan that ruled over the princely state of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan, India from the 12th to the 16th centuries. They were known as the Bhati Rajputs, and their rulers bore the title of Rawal. The Beighs were a prominent power in the region, and their territory extended beyond the modern-day boundaries of Jaisalmer.

The Beigh rulers were also known as the Badal Rajas, derived from their patron deity, the goddess Badal. They claimed descent from the legendary Rajput warrior Maharaja Prithviraj Chauhan. The Beighs were a warrior caste, and their military prowess was renowned. They built numerous forts and temples in their kingdom, including the famous Jaisalmer Fort.
